A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated proofs, figures, and experimental material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original AIHWKIT simulations, including synthetic least-squares optimization and MNIST/CIFAR classification experiments in Section 6 and Appendix K.

after.justification: V4 retains the original optimization and classification simulations, including accuracy tables, training curves, and sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: The residual-array updates and digital-buffer extension are retained. Section 5 specifies signed single-pulse transfer and buffer debiting for the existing threshold mechanism; this supplies procedural detail without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic least-squares data, MNIST, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100, with the same classification tasks and response-function scenarios. Moving the gamma ablation into the main text adds no coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding accuracy and ablation comparisons retain Digital SGD, Analog SGD, Tiki-Taka/Residual Learning, and their v2 variants as applicable. The added latency estimate uses the already studied Analog SGD comparator.

E3.justification: V3 Appendix K.3 specifies output range 20, output noise 0.1, and 8-bit input/output quantization. V4 Table 4 instead reports output bound 12, Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.06, 7-bit DAC, and 9-bit ADC. These are revised reported settings, without evidence establishing reruns. New Appendix E also specifies assumptions for latency estimation.

E4.justification: New Appendix E adds an analysis of the residual array's memory and latency overhead. Existing cycle-variation, response-function, and gamma sensitivity studies are retained; the gamma study moves from Appendix K.7 to Section 6.

E5.justification: Both versions state that simulations are repeated three times and report means and standard deviations. Appendix K retains the same description of randomness and statistical calculation.

E6.justification: V4 Table 3 adds estimated per-layer times: forward/backward 40.0 ns for both methods, and update 165.9 ns for Analog SGD versus 371.8 ns for Residual Learning. Existing accuracy-table entries and plotted results are unchanged; these estimates do not establish a new measured performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 4 restores missing gamma factors in the residual identity and hypergradient, explaining absorption of 2/gamma into the learning rate. Section 5 replaces the quadratic noise penalty with the general response-dependent penalty and defines its coefficient using expected absolute noise. The principal theorems and proofs are retained; Theorem 4's proof is relocated.

C1.justification: Contribution C3 changes Residual Learning from a novel algorithm framework to a novel theoretical framework explicitly leading to the previously proposed Tiki-Taka. This refines the novelty claim, while the central implicit-penalty, convergence, and hardware-extension claims remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix E discusses doubled analog-memory requirements, shared ADCs, parallel execution, and the claimed affordability of additional latency. This adds a substantive resource tradeoff interpretation. Existing convergence interpretations and the limitation concerning unmodeled hardware imperfections remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 adds project-code access information. Appendix K adds an explicit RPU configuration table, input-noise and input-bound disclosures, and a 32-pulse cap; Section 5 details threshold-transfer bookkeeping. Existing optimizer, architecture, learning-rate, and simulation-hardware information is largely retained.

R1.justification: V4 more explicitly credits the original Tiki-Taka when positioning Residual Learning's contribution. It also adds references [83] and [84] concerning memristor programming and accelerator architecture to support the overhead discussion. The broader literature coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: V4 makes distributed grammatical and terminology edits, expands several explanations, and updates affiliation and funding text. It moves the gamma ablation into Section 6 and the pulse-update proof into Appendix C, while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: V4 adds the latency and hardware-configuration tables. V3 Figure 6 becomes main-text Figure 5, and appendix tables are repositioned and renumbered. Existing graphical content is retained, with limited caption and layout changes.

improvement.justification: Corrected derivations, clearer transfer bookkeeping and prior-work credit, and added code-access and hardware details modestly improve precision and reproducibility. The gains are limited: accuracy evidence is unchanged, revised I/O settings are not reconciled with the retained scores, and the new latency comparison provides estimates rather than measured training costs.
